subject: Post-demo follow-up: competitive deltas + edge-case test plan
messages:
From: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwoodinference.com>
To: David Liu <david@cloudforge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: competitive deltas + edge-case test plan

Hi David — thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can prioritize the comparative tests you asked for.

Key deltas you mentioned on the call:
- Latency tail at 512 tokens (spikes for interactive prompts)
- Failure modes on numeric/temporal reasoning for multi-step instructions
- Occasional entity hallucinations when prompts contain ambiguous context
- Cost sensitivity for sustained burst traffic (20rpm+ for small responses)

What we propose as an actionable follow-up (short list):
1) Edge-case prompt battery (we'll run against Redwood hosted model and the hyperscaler endpoint you provided): 200 targeted prompts across the classes above (numeric chains, entity ambiguity, temporal shifts).
2) Hallucination measurement: label-based spot check (sample of 500 outputs) + automated entity consistency checks.
3) Latency-slice comparison at 64/256/512 tokens with p95/p99 breakdown and cold vs warm cache.
4) Cost/throughput run: 10k short responses to model real burst pricing and KV cache effects.

Attachments: I've added a starter set of edge-case prompts (edgecase_samples.csv) and a short initial-compare-summary.pdf with what we captured live. Full probe spec in the Drive link below.

As next steps — please confirm: (A) that we can run benchmark calls against the endpoint you shared (I'll need an API key or a short-lived test token), and (B) whether Procurement wants an initial SOW for the dedicated evaluation (we can keep it scoped to 2 weeks and a small compute budget).

I'll map owners on our side once you confirm. Suggested owners: Marissa (quality/evals) and Ben (perf/throughput).

Thanks,
Rafael
Rafael Mendes

Thanks Rafael — solid recap and exactly what we discussed. A few clarifications: 
- We'll provide a short-lived test token (scope: read-only, throttled) — give me the target IPs and estimated call pattern so SRE can create the token.
- For the latency runs, please include a warm-cache vs cold-cache delimiter. We care about p99 for interactive UX (sub-400ms target ideally).
- Procurement prefers an informal eval SOW first — a one-page statement with objectives, duration (2 weeks), and estimated compute hours should be fine.

Also: can you add a quick fuzz-suite that includes prompts with deliberately malformed dates (e.g., "April 31st") and half-complete references ("the CEO who joined in 20__")? Those tripped the hyperscaler model in earlier runs.

I'll send the token by EOD and confirm whether we want a shared sandbox network (VPN) or allow calls from Redwood public IPs.

Appreciate the fast turnaround,
David

Marissa / Ben — forwarding the thread. David will provide a short-lived test token later today; Procurement wants a one-page eval SOW.

Quick division of labor proposal (feel free to disagree):
- Marissa: Own the edge-case prompt battery, labeling plan, and hallucination metric (we should output a CSV with ground-truth vs model-output and a simple "hallucinated": yes/no column). Target: 500 labeled samples + 2k auto-scored probes. Deliverable: summary PDF + error examples.
- Ben: Perf runs and latency slicing. You'll run warm vs cold cache at 64/256/512 tokens and capture p50/p95/p99 and CPU/GPU utilization. Also capture burst-run cost estimate (10k short responses). Deliverable: CSV with latencies + a short cost model.

Two test specifics I want included (to keep differentiation focus measurable):
1) Entity anchoring test: provide the same ambiguous entity across 30 prompts and check for referent drift across responses — measure consistency score.
2) Numeric-chain hallucination test: 100 multi-step arithmetic/legal-logic style chains where the model must preserve internal numeric state; measure exact-match of final numeric answer and per-step consistency.

I've attached an initial prompt set and probe spec in the Drive link. Let's aim to have initial runs and a 1-page SOW to David by EOD tomorrow.

Also flag: if we see upstream data-retention or audit-log questions during the eval, loop Sofia (security) — I'll add her if needed.

Rafael

Sounds good — I'll start the latency slices this afternoon once David sends the token. A couple of practical notes from previous hyperscaler comparisons:
- Warm cache measurement: send 25 priming requests for each prompt shape then measure the next 200 calls. For cold cache, rotate instance IDs and measure first-call p99.
- For cost modeling: capture token counts, average response sizes, and GPU utilization. That plus the hyperscaler's invoiced per-inference cost gives a close estimate of end-user cost.

I'll push a small skeleton script to the shared Drive under /scripts/latency-slices.sh so Marissa can pair the probes with exact timing.

Ben
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
